newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CALL MONEY DIPS ON AMPLE LIQUIDITY PACT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CALL MONEY DIPS ON AMPLE LIQUIDITY PACT.

text.p: Overnight guilder rates slipped fractionally on Friday on the back of an ample liquidity allocation to the market under the latest special advances pact.
Call money was traded at around 3.18-3.25 percent towards the end of the session, a touch down from Thursday's levels, dealers said.
The Dutch central bank said early Friday it had allocated 4.75 billion guilders to the market under a seven-day liquidity pact at an unchanged rate of 3.0 percent.
Individual banks received 16.5 percent of the amount for which they had applied, up to a ceiling of 5.0 billion guilders.
"It was a reasonably generous allocation," one dealer said.
Another said the market had half expected a hike in the special advances rate, currently pegged at the level of Germany's equivalent repo rate.

He said current market rates were relatively out of line with the current 2.5 percent secured loans rate, but that the Dutch central bank had apparently decided to wait on any move by Germany's Bundesbank.
"The Buba will move on rates, I'm sure, but quite when is the question," he said.
The guilder was pegged at 112.675 per 100 marks on Friday.
This was a touch softer than its ERM central rate of 112.673 guilders per 100 marks.
